## 固定收益市場主線

美國通膨降溫，降低了聯準會近期升息的可能性，卻未能阻止9月30日長天期美國公債再度下跌。彭博每日殖利率資料顯示，30年期殖利率升至5.64%，為2002年以來首見，10年期則達5.29%。消費支出強勁、民間就業增加，維持了經濟成長的支撐；企業大量融資也持續爭取長期資金。市場對10月政策決定稍感寬心，不代表數十年期的借款成本隨之下降。

季底的固定收益市場表現日益分化。10年期市政債創下一年多來最強漲勢，體質最弱的企業債利差卻跨越困境債券門檻。Paramount完成龐大的收購融資，優先順位債券的發行利差雖然收窄，殖利率仍相當高。歐洲最新公布的各國通膨高於預期，使ECB仍須權衡進一步升息的時點；中國景氣小幅回升，卻尚未顯示國內信貸需求出現明確轉變。

## PCE降溫改變聯準會升息時點，未帶動長債需求

美國8月核心個人消費支出物價指數（PCE）月增0.2%，低於市場預期的0.3%，7月月增率則下修至0.1%。數據公布後，短天期美國公債率先受惠，2年期殖利率一度下降5個基點至4.82%，為一週多來最低，隨後又收回大部分跌幅。利率交換市場將聯準會10月升息機率由原先約五成降至約36%。

年增率的修訂也相當顯著：8月核心PCE年增3%，連續第三個月維持此水準，7月原公布的3.3%也下修至3%。整體PCE年增3.4%，與修訂後的7月相同，月增0.3%。美國經濟分析局這次納入回溯五年的年度修訂，並調整通膨計算方法。道明證券的Gennadiy Goldberg認為，較溫和的數據舒緩了眼前的通膨焦慮，但統計調整仍有不確定性，投資人因此不願進一步推升債市。

細項並不像核心指標那樣全面令人安心。商品與服務價格均上漲，包含汽油、運輸服務、餐飲及住宿；排除能源與住宅的服務價格月增0.4%，為5月以來最快。TradeStation的David Russell也指出，8月資料尚未反映9月柴油價格急升。通膨水準經修訂後下降，讓決策者有更多時間觀察，但無論年度修訂或單月低於預期，都不足以判定能源成本的後續轉嫁已經結束。

需求反而增強。8月名目個人消費支出月增0.9%，高於預期的0.8%，也明顯超過下修後7月的0.1%；實質支出增加0.6%，創2025年3月以來最大月增幅。消費不只集中在必需品，汽車、家具、服飾、餐飲與住宿支出都增加。這樣的廣度對成長前景的意義，大於單純由燃料帳單上升帶來的名目支出增加。

所得卻沒有跟上。個人所得月增0.2%，低於預期的0.4%及修訂後前月的0.3%；實質可支配所得持平，為4月以來最弱，儲蓄率降至4.1%，為2022年以來最低。年度修訂顯示，家庭的財務緩衝比先前估計更充裕，但8月消費增速仍超過當期購買力。Navy Federal Credit Union的Heather Long認為，支出與所得的落差正在考驗消費者能否持續保持韌性。

修訂後的成長數據同樣凸顯需求強度。第2季GDP經季節調整後的年化成長率為2.2%，高於市場預期的1.5%，也由先前公布的1.5%上修，主要來自投資、消費與政府支出；第1季成長也獲上修。第2季消費支出增速是2024年底以來最快。歷史成長估計上調，加上8月實際消費增加，強化了經濟能承受限制性借款成本的信心。

較新的9月ADP資料則顯示，民間就業增加9萬人，為三個月最多，高於預期的7萬人；8月由3.8萬人下修至3.6萬人。ADP數據尚不足以推斷週五官方就業報告的結果，但使「招聘放緩已演變為加速萎縮」的說法較難成立。在通膨降溫帶動短債最初上漲後，民間就業與消費數據共同支撐成長判斷，也推動長債殖利率再度走高。

週三盤中，30年期殖利率一度上升6個基點至5.63%，為2002年以來最高。牛津經濟研究院的John Canavan認為，較強的經濟活動數據，加上投資人不願在非農就業公布前大幅調整部位，使曲線更趨陡峭。Natixis利率策略師John Briggs觀察到實際買盤偏弱；Fort Washington的Dan Carter則認為，已押注殖利率下降的投資人，可能沒有太多餘力再買進債券。這些觀察解釋了為何10月升息機率降低，仍能與長端持續下跌並存。

彭博9月30日每日資料顯示，2年期殖利率為4.89%，上升1.2個基點；10年期為5.29%，上升5.3個基點；30年期為5.64%，上升7.2個基點。2年與10年期利差擴大4.1個基點至40個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大6個基點至75個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升2.4個基點至2.915%，損益兩平通膨率上升2.9個基點至2.375%。因此，當天名目殖利率上升同時反映實質借款成本與通膨補償增加，並非只有其中一項推動。

政策預期的變化主要在下一次會議，而非整個升息週期。通膨資料公布，加上紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams週二釋出耐心觀察的訊息後，高盛經濟學家將下一次升息預測由10月延至12月。不過，交易員仍預期未來一年至少升息三次。PNC首席經濟學家Gus Faucher認為，聯準會目前可以等待，但仍預期之後會繼續升息。新公布的通膨與景氣數據，促成了這次政策預期調整。

房貸市場已顯示緊縮對家庭的影響。美國房貸銀行協會資料指出，截至9月25日當週，30年期固定房貸合約利率上升18個基點至7.30%，連續第六週走高，並創2023年11月以來最高；5年期可調利率房貸利率上升37個基點至6.47%，為兩年多來最高。購屋貸款申請減少4.3%，降至2025年4月以來最低；轉貸申請再減8.7%，延續8月中旬以來的下滑。

First American經濟學家Mark Fleming指出，既有房貸利率多為3%或4%，新貸款則超過7%，兩者落差擴大將使更多屋主留在原屋。他預期房價不易下跌，前提是沒有重大衰退迫使屋主出售。因此，眼前受到壓抑的是交易與轉貸活動，房價不一定按相同比例下降。整體消費強勁，仍可與利率敏感產業明顯受限並存。

油價也讓8月的通膨降溫難以直接外推。固定收益交易時段結束時，WTI為$90.16，上漲0.87%；布蘭特原油為$103.58，上漲0.97%。摩根大通最新航運估計顯示，中東原油出口的10日平均量達每日1,750萬桶，恢復至戰前的98%；高盛另行評估也認為，流量正回歸正常。這項改善顯示，不只已恢復運作的沙烏地阿拉伯管線，整體出口也有更廣泛的復甦，但航運風險仍使實際供應與能源價格不穩。

伊拉克國營石油銷售商的定價反映了復甦並不均衡。其10月合約原油供應相對區域基準每桶最高折價$37，以吸引買家，彌補伊拉克距離荷姆茲海峽較遠所帶來的航運困難。總出口量回升，不代表個別生產國的物流劣勢已消失。美股也未能維持通膨公布後的初步漲勢：標普500盤中一度上漲0.7%，終場反跌0.25%；那斯達克100則上漲0.23%。

## 歐洲通膨超預期，財政與融資風險並存

德國、法國與義大利最新通膨均加速，顯示歐洲能源衝擊的範圍持續擴大。德國9月年增率升至3.3%，高於預測中位數3.2%，並創近三年最高，主要由能源推動；該國基礎通膨指標仍為2.4%。勞動需求偏弱，在通常會出現夏季後招聘的月份，失業人數反而增加，暫未明顯支持薪資帶動物價加速的判斷。

法國年增率升至3.4%，為兩年多來最快；義大利達4.1%，為2023年以來最高，兩者皆超過預期。法國能源成本年增21.2%，壓力也不完全限於燃料：服務通膨由1.9%升至2.2%，食品由1.1%升至1.5%，其中熱浪後生鮮農產品價格上漲。這些細項使「純粹是孤立的能源衝擊」不再足以概括現況，但尚不能證明全面性的薪資與物價螺旋已形成。

ECB的爭論仍圍繞這項區別。彭博經濟研究的Simona Delle Chiaie預期目前維持利率，12月再作最後一次升息；她認為關鍵在能源是否傳導至核心通膨，目前證據仍有限。立場較偏鴿派的希臘央行總裁Yannis Stournaras與馬爾他央行總裁Alexander Demarco都未排除10月升息，與傾向12月的經濟學家及交易員形成對照。各國最新數據強化了今年再升息的理由，時間卻仍未定。

德國公債週三歐洲交易時段仍上漲，沒有隨通膨超預期而下跌。2年期殖利率下降8個基點至3.22%，10年期下降6個基點至3.57%。市場認為ECB在10月29日升息25個基點的機率約三分之一，同時仍反映明年秋季前最高約90個基點的緊縮。LB Macro的Simon Harvey不同意近期機率如此低，基於通膨數據與能源前景，他自己的估計接近50%。眼前升息步調較緩，並不排除較長期間仍有大幅緊縮。

法國公債表現落後於這波漲勢。10年期相對德國的利差略高於120個基點，OAT殖利率比同天期義大利公債高22個基點，為歐元區成立以來最大差距。最新惡化一方面伴隨通膨意外上升，另一方面民調顯示，明年總統決選可能由Marine Le Pen與Jean-Luc Melenchon對決。Natixis策略師Theophile Legrand將政治風險溢價升高與該民調連結。法國10年期殖利率本季上升1.15個百分點至4.8%，為至少1999年以來最差的季度表現。

ECB總裁Christine Lagarde週三受訪時，反對Melenchon取消央行持有債務的主張，認為財務上危險、技術上也有不確定性。她警告，不償還債務可能使貸方卻步，或要求更高利率，且將違反歐洲條約。Lagarde也保留在2027年10月任期屆滿前幾個月離任的可能性，但表示2027年仍會在任，尚未宣布具體離任時間。

義大利則面臨另一項待定的財政選擇。總理Giorgia Meloni表示，將向歐盟執委會爭取更多預算彈性，以援助能源帳單上升的家庭與企業，並計畫在下週盧森堡財長會議及之後的歐盟理事會提出。2025年赤字已確認為GDP的3.1%，使義大利仍受過度赤字程序約束，增加援助更為複雜。借款限制尚未獲准放寬，但在市場融資成本攀升之際，能源通膨已讓財政支持重新進入討論。

波蘭9月初估通膨由3.4%升至4%，符合預測中位數，卻創15個月新高，也超出央行2.5%上下1個百分點的目標範圍。燃料成本增加及價格上限結束都是壓力來源。總裁Adam Glapinski原本傾向今年維持3.75%，甚至可能延續至2027年中；貨幣政策委員Ludwik Kotecki則認為10月可開始討論，若預測顯示通膨將更長時間高於4%，11月可能升息。ING Bank Slaski與Bank Pekao都已改為預期升息，茲羅提週三對歐元升值0.2%。

英格蘭銀行季度金融穩定評估提出了不同於通膨的融資風險。避險基金在英國公債的槓桿維持穩定，卻仍偏高；央行警告，主權債、企業債與AI相關資產相互連結，可能使多項脆弱環節同時出現問題。英鎊貨幣市場資料顯示，英國公債附買回交易商對非銀行金融機構的淨現金放款，自2023年以來倍增至£2,000億。非銀行金融機構愈依賴以英國公債作擔保取得資金，被迫解除槓桿部位時，就愈可能將壓力傳至其他市場。

英格蘭銀行也警告，AI估值的修正可能比7月更劇烈。當時雖有解除部位與去槓桿，並未外溢至核心市場；現在則因經濟成長預期部分依賴AI生產力，重新評估可能不只衝擊科技股，也波及主權債。部分私募信貸市場同樣容易受到融資條件收緊影響。不過，央行仍認為家庭具韌性、銀行資本充足，市場脆弱性並不等於銀行體系已受損。

進一步分析支持了英格蘭銀行7月提出放寬銀行絕對槓桿上限的建議。官員認為，計畫中的英國公債市場改革更適合處理這些融資風險，擬於2027年初展開諮詢，同時保留風險改變時將槓桿比率緩衝提高25個基點的選項。這並非認定槓桿不再重要，而是優先以特定市場改革應對，不自動收緊銀行整體資產負債表的限制。

最新股票分析也呈現了跨市場調整的可能性。Macro Risk Advisors發現，個股波動與指數平靜程度的落差，是2000年網路泡沫崩潰以來最大。Cboe的Mandy Xu表示，標普500中規模最大的100檔股票，約40%出現買權偏斜反轉，顯示上漲方向需求異常強。Macro Risk Advisors的Dean Curnutt認為，若資料中心債務疑慮導致AI支出縮減，原本互相抵銷的個股漲跌可能轉為同步下跌。

## Paramount完成融資，其他發行人調整條件爭取資金

銀行完成了Paramount Skydance收購Warner Bros. Discovery所需約$520億的聯貸與債券銷售，將本週持續變動的訂單轉成長期資金。知情人士表示，公司出售$300億美元投資等級債、等值$124億的高收益債，並取得$94.6億貸款，由Apollo、美國銀行與花旗主導。這筆$1,100億收購案成功籌得融資，但絕對借款成本異常高。

八券組成的優先順位債券在銷售過程中收窄了殖利率利差，2066年到期券仍提供接近9%的殖利率。三檔優先順位債的殖利率超過8%，相較之下，今年稍早全美只有兩檔投資等級債以如此高的殖利率發行。發行利差在銷售期間收窄，與長期基準利率仍偏高是兩回事；利差收窄無法抵銷基準資金成本的上升。

非投資等級部分包括三券共$114億的美元債，以及€8.85億的5年期債。10年期美元券殖利率約9.13%，歐元券以7%定價，先前的8年期歐元券則已取消。不同於優先順位債利差收窄，高收益債的定價大致符合最初洽談水準。完成的貸款包含$85億美元與€8.5億，兩者利率均為各自基準加2.75個百分點。

最終條件讓Paramount原已艱鉅的降槓桿任務更為具體。CreditSights指出，收購後債務將超過$870億，公司三年內達成每年節省$60億的目標，必須支撐這筆債務。昂貴融資能否負擔，將取決於這些營運與財務條件。優先順位債的評等也有分歧：惠譽與標普給予投資等級，穆迪卻連第一順位擔保債都評為非投資等級。因此，龐大的投資等級發債規模，不代表各評等機構一致看好合併後借款人的槓桿與營運落實能力。

其他發行人透過調整結構取得資金，不只是接受更高的優先順位債殖利率。Clearlake與投資人討論後，修改擔保資產並降低槓桿，以基金擔保債務工具（collateralized fund obligation）籌得$10億。工具持有$6億私募信貸曝險、$2億私募股權次級交易基金及另一筆$2億私募股權基金權益，對應發行A、B、C級債務合計$7.75億及$2.25億股權，由高盛獨家負責結構設計與銷售。

最安全的Clearlake債券以SOFR加285個基點定價，較初步定價低15個基點；C級支付SOFR加800個基點，承擔最先損失的股權部分預期內部報酬率約18%。投資人曾反對原先由三檔信貸基金及兩檔其他私募基金組成架構的槓桿，最安全級別的利差收窄，反映擔保資產與資本結構經過實質調整，而不只是原有條件下認購需求轉強。這項證券化也使保險公司能取得基金曝險，部分曝險原本可能因屬私募股權而無法直接持有。

Remy Cointreau首次發行混合資本債，在推動轉型之際維護投資等級評等。其€2.5億次順位債首次可贖回日在五年後，以6.75%定價，低於初步指引的7%至7.25%。訂單超過€6.95億，為發行規模的2.7倍以上。穆迪給予這家烈酒集團Baa3及負向展望，因此即使混合資本債成本高於一般優先順位債，部分金額可被認列為股權的評等待遇仍特別有價值。

取得這項股權認列的相對成本，也比歷史水準有利。ICE指數資料顯示，混合資本債相對優先順位債的平均溢酬約74個基點，長期平均則接近120個基點。即使第1季銷售成長優於預期，Remy仍面臨干邑與高階烈酒需求疲弱、關稅及飲酒習慣改變。執行長Franck Marilly的轉型與產品組合檢討必須處理這些營運壓力；混合資本債改變的是融資在評等中的認列，不是解決營運問題。

Platinum Equity收購雀巢飲用水事業股權的融資，則讓槓桿貸款債權人取得更明確的契約保障。最新披露的€28億交易條件包含omniblocker條款，旨在阻止只優待部分債權人、犧牲其他債權人的交易。美國銀行與德意志銀行主導的銀行團，把歐元及美元貸款利差最多提高1個百分點，至基準加4個百分點；7年期貸款以面額97%出售。這項由雙方共同持有、現名Peranel的事業，其債務已於週五定價。

這項保障在收購融資中並不常見，也不只是價格讓利，而是針對日後負債管理交易可能改變債權人相對待遇的風險。投資人同時獲得更強的契約保護與較高補償。另一筆證券化交易則由Polar Asset Management推出C$4.3億加拿大住宅房貸抵押證券White Bear RMBS I LP, Series 2026-1，認購超額。擔保資產為未投保的第一順位固定利率房貸，加權平均貸款成數71.1%，由CMLS Financial負責貸款服務。即使無擔保與高槓桿借款人的條件變得昂貴，特定擔保資產仍能吸引需求。

## 市政債買盤回流，體質較弱企業的信用惡化

市政債結束近兩週的跌勢，與長天期美國公債形成鮮明對照。紐約時間下午4時，指標10年期市政債價格錄得2025年4月以來最大漲幅，也是9月17日以來首次上漲，殖利率下降11個基點至4.11%；30年期殖利率下降6個基點至5.19%。Belle Haven的Dora Lee認為，這是超賣後的修正，但聯準會仍有進一步升息的可能，漲勢能否持續尚難確定。

反彈開始讓初級市場重啟。那什維爾與戴維森郡會展中心管理局在前一週延後定價後，推出約$7.9億債券，規模略高於先前計畫。Cavanal Hill的Leslie Martin表示，絕對殖利率吸引買家回流。最新資金流資料也顯示，過去一個月逾$30億流入Vanguard的VTEB市政債ETF，為2022年以來最強月度流入。這些需求是在市場仍承受9月罕見的大幅損失時出現，不是等價格穩定後才進場。

企業信用最弱的一端卻走向相反方向。CCC級債券週三相對美國公債利差達1,007個基點，高於9月初的860個基點，也是2023年3月銀行危機以來，首次突破通常用來界定困境債券的1,000個基點門檻。美國整體高收益債利差當天僅小幅擴大，CCC的惡化卻遠比整體描述嚴重，凸顯了最容易受高利率再融資影響的借款人。

嘉信理財的Collin Martin認為，經濟表現雖然尚可，強度卻不足以消除最弱發行人對借款成本的敏感性。規模較小的高槓桿企業若無法轉嫁成本，承受昂貴能源的空間也更有限。巴克萊發現，CCC內部分化明顯，表現最差者有超過一半來自科技、媒體與電信，尤其有線電視與衛星業者。CCC占高收益債指數約8.5%，低於一年前的9.7%；較高評等利差相對穩定。因此，惡化是集中發生，並非平均擴散至所有企業信用。

泳池用品零售商Leslie's已正式進入重整。公司週三在德州南區提出預先協商的美國破產法第11章申請，支持協議擬削減約$6.85億、相當於九成的債務，並將控制權移交債權人。協議包含$9,000萬新增資金的破產程序中債務人融資（DIP）承諾。公司計畫維持正常營運，力求於2027年初完成重整，同時宣布關閉76家門市，並繼續檢討據點配置。

Leslie's先前延長到期日的嘗試未成功，之後與包括Grey Helm、Axar、Cerberus及Contrarian在內的債權人協商，最終提出申請。天候干擾、投入成本提高及家庭財務壓力都使泳池產業受挫。公司在申請書列示資產$5億至$10億、負債$10億至$100億。新增融資與擬議減債將透過法院程序處理資產負債表，而非只是將還款挪到更晚年度。

Hertz則尋求較溫和的方式。知情人士表示，PJT Partners近幾週已接觸債務投資人，討論可能的修改條款並延長期限交易。Hertz有一筆票息4.63%、金額$2億的債券於12月1日到期，另有$27億貸款在2028年到期。公司8月公布的流動性接近$10億，超過12月到期金額，因此洽談並不代表已無力支付該筆債務。不過，車輛折舊沉重、財務波動大，使任何更廣泛展期的條件都很重要。

Brightline調整了對企業債債權人的重整安排。週三提交的文件給予這些投資人至少4.75%的重整後公司股權、治理權、可增加持股的認股權證，以及優先向未來Brightline實體提出注資方案的權利。企業債約$11億、利率11%，仰賴約$22億優先順位市政債受償後剩餘的收入，最初未被納入重整方案。新的股權與參與權，是對不同意原方案的次順位債權人作出的具體讓步。

最新報導也指出，Diameter Capital Partners、Redwood Capital與FourSixThree Capital買下了Nuveen以面額45%出售、約$1.9億的優先順位未投保市政債組合。週三該債務成交價為面額55%。價格回升發生在先前已披露的整批出售之後，沒有改變已完成交易的條件。Brightline計畫另包含Assured Guaranty與其他市政債投資人提供的$2.58億破產融資。企業債債權人待遇改善，與優先順位債價格變動，是資本結構不同層級的兩項進展。

銀行監管則有獨立的制度變化。聯準會理事會以6比1通過兩項最終壓力測試規則，要求測試情境及重大模型變更徵詢公眾意見，並更新情境架構、時程及全球市場衝擊項目。自2028年起，連續兩年參加測試的銀行，其壓力資本緩衝將採最近兩次年度測試的平均值。聯準會估計，資本要求的年度波動可降低約50%，整體資本要求則不會有重大變化。

負責監管的副主席Michelle Bowman表示，透過更透明、細緻且對風險更敏感的測試，架構仍能維持韌性。理事Michael Barr投下反對票，認為規則將大幅削弱測試與銀行韌性。聯準會另外徵詢意見，探討如何更妥善反映銀行手續費收入商業模式的差異。決定改變的是資本要求跨年度的演變方式，爭點則是提高可預測性，是否會犧牲測試揭露風險的能力。

聯準會總部整修也再度引發治理爭議。內部監察長未發現刑事違法或行政失當，但指出管理疏失使成本由2020年最初編列的$13億增加至$24億。總統川普要求前主席Jerome Powell辭去理事職務，並請司法部長Todd Blanche檢視調查結果。主席Kevin Warsh表示，聯準會將落實建議、任命獨立成本稽核人員，並交由聯邦總務署負責工程執行。監察報告確認了監督不足，但並未證實刑事指控。

## 亞洲景氣與新興市場政策各走其路

中國9月景氣調查改善，卻未使債市出現相應的重新定價。官方製造業PMI由49.8升至50.1，符合預期，為6月以來首次重回擴張；非製造業指數意外升至50.2，營建活動也結束連續八個月下降。RatingDog製造業指數升至52.1，增幅超過預期並創五個月新高，服務業指數由51.4升至51.6。官方與民間調查均改善，但民間製造業樣本對出口韌性的反應較明顯。

數據及最新定向支持措施公布後，國債與人民幣大致持平，週三10年期國債殖利率約1.67%。新政策細節包括將1年期抵押補充貸款利率降低25個基點至1.5%，並增加人民幣2,000億元科技創新與設備更新再貸款額度。這些措施針對特定領域降低融資成本或增加資金，不是宣布全面調降市場利率。

反應有限，因為能取得較便宜的信貸，不等於願意借款。Yingke Zhou領銜的巴克萊經濟學家認為，主要限制是信貸需求，而非價格。先前公布、針對合格買方的房貸補貼將於10月1日上路，面積與價值資格上限使受惠集中在較低線城市。摩根士丹利的Robin Xing認為，家庭去槓桿及土地收入疲弱對地方政府的壓力，可能限制政策效果。9月景氣改善，與旨在守住成長底線的政策並存，尚不能視為房市全面復甦的證據。

中國附買回市場則在債券需求的另一面有所進展。境外機構8月附買回交易量為人民幣1.2兆元，超過一年前人民幣5,730億元的兩倍。外資持有約人民幣3.2兆元境內債券，新增的融資管道提高了以這些證券取得流動性的能力。買斷式附買回會轉移所有權，而不是將擔保品凍結在賣方帳戶，其占外資交割量23%，一年前約為4%。

參與仍然有限。境外投資人持有約2%的境內債券，附買回交易量卻只占全市場1.2%。選擇英格蘭法管轄的全球協議或中國法管轄的本地契約，會在破產處理、作業規則及終止淨額結算上產生摩擦。Ashurst Perkins Coie的Priscilla Chen表示，全球附買回交易主契約（GMRA）通常需洽談三至六個月。中國殖利率偏低也限制外資需求，市場開放與擔保品運用的改善，比債券報酬對國際投資人的吸引力提升更快。

巴西礦商Vale考慮首次發行熊貓債，則顯示低殖利率市場對借款人的吸引力。公司擬籌措最高人民幣35億元、約$5.22億，於10月19日當週路演，最快11月銷售；可能採3年、5年及10年期，仍待投資人回饋。發行人將是Vale Overseas，由母公司擔保。今年企業與主權熊貓債發行量已達人民幣2,450億元，增加78%，平均票息1.88%，為歷來最低。中國約占Vale營收一半，擬議交易可分散其融資來源，目前尚未完成發行。

日本2年期公債標售則提供了實際需求觀察。投標倍數由前次2.97倍升至3.89倍，高於過去12個月平均3.75倍；平均與最低得標價格的差距由0.034縮至0.014。結果公布後，期貨收斂跌幅，2年期殖利率下降1.5個基點至1.945%。SMBC日興的Miki Den認為，高殖利率帶來良好認購，即使日本央行仍可能再升息，買家仍願意進場。週三隔夜利率交換反映10月升息機率約23%，12月前升息25個基點則幾乎已完全反映。

澳洲最新房市與通膨資料，使繼續升息的限制更為鮮明。8月通膨達4%，高於澳洲央行2%至3%的目標；Cotality同時報告，全國住宅價格連續第六個月下降，較3月高峰低5.2%。雪梨較2月高峰跌8.6%，墨爾本較11月高峰跌7.2%。八個首府有七個下跌，僅達爾文例外，首府以外地區仍上漲；雪梨與墨爾本高價住宅已較高峰跌逾10%。

家庭對利率的敏感度相當高：債務約為年度可支配所得的178%，多數房貸採浮動利率。澳洲聯邦銀行指出，5月以來整體房貸申請減少15%，投資用房貸申請減少28%。自2027年7月起，負扣稅扣除額將限於新建住宅，資本利得的50%折扣則改以通膨調整後的購入價格取代。這些已宣布、尚待實施的稅制改變，將與目前4.6%現金利率的作用一道，進一步約束投資需求。

對房價跌幅的預測仍有分歧。西太平洋銀行的Matthew Hassan預期全國高峰至谷底跌7.3%，澳洲聯邦銀行的Trent Saunders估9%，匯豐的Paul Bloxham則估13%，雪梨跌幅17%。施羅德週二買進3年期債券，其澳洲固定收益主管Kellie Wood預期，隨通膨衝擊逐步發酵、成長風險變得更重要，2027年將開始寬鬆。Aberdeen的Adam McCabe仍因通膨持續而預期再升息，並希望看到更明確的經濟轉弱。最新房市數據增加了成長限制的份量，並未消除通膨高於目標的事實。

印度資產則受較不利的外部條件壓抑。外資9月賣出$11億符合指數納入資格的主權債，在6月創紀錄流入之後，料將出現3月以來最大單月流出；股票也在連續兩個月買超後遭賣出$21億。10年期主權債殖利率本週達兩年新高。印度仰賴進口，油價上升構成負擔；已開發市場殖利率走高，也削弱當地報酬的競爭力，並提高匯率避險成本。Aberdeen的Fesa Wibawa認為，賣壓主要是全球債市修正的一環，而非全面重新評估印度。

儘管銀行透過特別海外僑民存款計畫吸收$1,330億，資金仍撤離。這些美元與印度央行進行交換，一度將外匯存底推至創紀錄的$7,857億，但央行仍持續賣出美元支撐盧比。強烈聖嬰現象下，季風降雨為十多年來最差，對農作物、水庫及食品價格增添另一項風險。外部緩衝加強，與當前外資賣壓及新出現的國內供應疑慮並存，使政策支持更複雜。

哥倫比亞意外升息25個基點至12.25%，為2024年以來最高。四位理事支持該幅度，兩位主張不變，一位要求升50個基點。29名分析師中，22名預期維持、五名預期升50個基點，只有兩名預測實際採取的幅度。總裁Leonardo Villar表示，限制性政策與2027年通膨下降的路徑一致；8月通膨已加速至6.24%，遠高於3%上下1個百分點的目標。

這次升息發生在景氣轉弱而非成長加速之際。8月都市失業率意外升至9.1%，7月經濟活動、製造業及零售銷售都不如預期。財長Miguel Gomez首次出席政策會議，投資人仍在等待承諾的財政削減細節。政府警告明年赤字可能超過GDP的9%，並與IMF磋商，財政可信度仍對通膨前景重要。即使經濟降溫已更明顯，多數理事仍選擇加強抑制需求。

尚比亞則大幅走向另一方向。總裁Denny Kalyalya宣布利率由13.25%降至10.75%，為連續第四次降息，也是至少2012年以來最大幅度。9月通膨由6.2%降至6.1%，預測顯示至2028年都將落在6%至8%的目標區間。年度平均通膨預測下調約1個百分點，今年為6.7%、明年6%，2028年上半年6.3%。克瓦查升值近13%，加上穀物價格預期穩定，支持了這項展望。

尚比亞外匯存底由6月的$58億升至7月底的$60億，可支應4.5個月進口，礦業稅收與專案資金流入有所貢獻。央行預估今年成長5.3%、2027年6%、2028年7.1%。有利的預測仍面臨聖嬰現象及中東衝突的重要風險，且燃料稅暫緩措施與加值稅零稅率待遇在9月30日到期。這次大幅降息所依據的國內通膨與匯率條件，與哥倫比亞不同。

斯里蘭卡連續第二次維持隔夜利率8.75%，符合受訪11位經濟學家中六位的預期，其餘預期升息25至50個基點。央行表示，先前緊縮已發揮效果，中期通膨預期仍穩定，儘管8月通膨8%，高於5%的目標。央行預測至2027年第1季仍為高個位數通膨，之後逐步向目標收斂；若壓力加劇或預期穩定性轉弱，隨時準備行動。第2季成長由5.1%放緩至4.2%，能源進口風險與復甦放緩，同時牽制政策選擇。

莫三比克也按兵不動，連續第四次維持Mimo利率9.25%。新任總裁Felisberto Navalha指出，即使8月通膨降至6.5%，能源、氣候及成長疲弱仍有風險。近幾個月柴油零售價格上漲逾40%，外匯短缺也干擾進口。財政部預期今年成長僅0.6%，薪資與債務服務支出將占2027年收入96%。IMF資助計畫可能要求提高匯率彈性，標普預期至2029年梅蒂卡爾溫和貶值，可能再添物價壓力。

加彭則委任美國銀行，週三開始為擬議的$5.8億美元債舉行投資人會議，最終到期年限8年，距離上次籌得$9.2億僅兩個月。發行正值加彭洽談有資金支持的IMF計畫。倫敦時間下午12時26分，其2031年債下跌1.2美分至84.3，連續第六日下跌；2029年券跌0.7美分至94.4。預算草案規劃在國際市場借款非洲金融共同體法郎1.1兆、約$19億，引發新一輪壓力，抵銷了先前審計顯示債務比原估低約五分之一所帶來的樂觀。

較高評等的新興市場借款人，也擴展其他幣別融資。截至週一，瑞士法郎發債約$39億，接近2025年同期的三倍，但相較整體以主要國際貨幣籌資$6,100億，規模仍小。智利首次發行兩券共CHF3.8億，建立5年與10年期基準，需求幾乎全來自瑞士投資人。Gramercy的Petar Atanasov認為，A級及BBB級借款人最容易取得這個市場的資金；Aberdeen的Viktor Szabo則指出，美元避險後，低名目票息的部分優勢可能消失。幣別分散增加融資選項，仍無法取代規模更深的美元與歐元市場。

## 後續市場觀察

10月1日紐約時間上午10時公布的製造業ISM，預期由54.6升至55，將檢驗9月就業改善與較強消費是否延伸至工廠活動。週五上午8時30分的官方就業報告，預期9月非農就業增加9萬人，前月為16.2萬人；失業率預期維持4.1%。ADP最新結果優於預期，使官方就業增長的廣度更值得注意。若再度展現韌性，將支持經濟能承受高利率的判斷；若明顯轉弱，則會挑戰推升長端殖利率的成長假設。

10月5日上午10時接著公布服務業ISM，目前預測由55.4降至54。PCE細項顯示消費與服務價格仍強，因此服務業的意義不同於製造業。所得增速落後於消費、房貸成本提高又限制房屋交易，接下來要看需求是否能延續。這些數據都會在10月28日聯準會決策前公布；週三近期升息機率雖下降，後續升息預期並未消失。

週五歐元區通膨預期為3.7%，德國、法國與義大利最新結果高於預期，使上行風險增加。對ECB在10月或12月升息的選擇而言，核心通膨與更廣泛的成本傳導證據，比另一次只由能源推動的整體通膨上升更重要。法國10月1日提出預算，則是獨立的主權債考驗：OAT相對德國公債利差已略高於120個基點，預算內容及政治反應必須回應投資人對融資路徑的疑慮，而不只是歐洲整體通膨前景。

美國財政部計畫週四買回最高$60億、剩餘期限10至20年的證券。過去長期券買回實際承接量低於公告上限，因此此次實際買回規模關係到流動性效果。富國銀行的Angelo Manolatos表示，買回的影響主要在流動性與利差；長期利率若要持續下降，可能仍需負面的成長催化因素。

企業焦點如今由Paramount的債券行銷轉向已取得融資的負擔；Brightline承諾的股權與參與權，仍是法院監督下重整退出方案的一部分。週三市政債反彈，也讓先前延後發行的借款人有新的定價機會，那什維爾重返市場就是眼前例子。與CCC債陷入困境的對照顯示，需求能否延續取決於借款人及條件，並非固定收益市場已普遍復甦。

能源仍須獨立觀察。最新估計原油出口恢復至戰前98%，能否在航運風險下維持，仍是關鍵；伊拉克大幅折價也顯示，總流量恢復並未解決所有交付限制。即使已有出口回升估計，油價週三仍上漲，當前燃料衝擊的影響因此不會止於較溫和的8月通膨。成本舒緩是否傳到成品油，再傳到家庭與企業，將影響央行能把下一次升息延後多久。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Long Treasuries fell again on September 30 even as softer U.S. inflation reduced the likelihood of an immediate Federal Reserve increase. The 30-year yield reached 5.64%, a level last seen in 2002, while the 10-year stood at 5.29% in Bloomberg's daily observations. Strong consumer spending and firmer private hiring kept the growth case intact, and heavy corporate financing continued to compete for long-term capital. Relief over October's policy decision did not deliver relief in the cost of borrowing for decades.

The quarter ended with increasingly distinct outcomes across fixed income. Municipal bonds staged their strongest 10-year rally in more than a year, but the weakest corporate borrowers crossed a distressed-spread threshold. Paramount completed its enormous acquisition financing at expensive yields despite narrower senior-bond premiums. In Europe, fresh national inflation overshoots left the ECB weighing the timing of further tightening, while China reported a modest activity rebound without a convincing change in domestic credit demand.

## Softer PCE Changes Fed Timing, Not Long-Bond Demand

The first U.S. inflation response favored shorter Treasuries. August core personal consumption expenditures prices increased 0.2% from July, below the 0.3% consensus, while the preceding month's increase was revised to 0.1%. Two-year yields fell as much as 5 basis points to 4.82%, their lowest in just over a week, before giving back much of that decline. Interest-rate swaps reduced the probability of an October Fed increase to about 36% after the release, from roughly even odds beforehand.

The revision to the annual inflation picture was substantial. Core PCE inflation was 3% in August, its third consecutive month at that rate, with July revised down from 3.3%. Headline inflation was 3.4% annually, matching the revised July reading, and prices rose 0.3% over the month. The Bureau of Economic Analysis release incorporated annual revisions reaching back five years and changes to inflation methodology. TD Securities' Gennadiy Goldberg said the softer reading relieved immediate inflation anxiety, although uncertainty over the statistical changes restrained investors' willingness to extend the rally.

The details were less uniformly reassuring than the core headline. Prices increased for both goods and services, including gasoline, transportation services, food services and accommodation. Services inflation excluding energy and housing rose 0.4%, its fastest monthly increase since May. TradeStation's David Russell also noted that August's observation preceded September's diesel-price surge. The lower revised inflation level gave policymakers more time, but neither that revision nor a single monthly undershoot settled the question of continuing energy pass-through.

Demand, meanwhile, strengthened. Nominal personal spending increased 0.9% in August, above the 0.8% consensus and a revised 0.1% increase in July. Inflation-adjusted spending rose 0.6%, the largest monthly gain since March 2025. Purchases extended beyond necessities: households increased spending on motor vehicles, furnishings and clothing, as well as restaurants and accommodation. That breadth made the release more consequential for the growth outlook than a nominal increase driven solely by higher fuel bills.

Income did not keep pace. Personal income rose 0.2%, against a 0.4% consensus and a revised 0.3% increase previously. Real disposable income was flat, its weakest result since April, while the saving rate fell to 4.1%, the lowest since 2022. Annual revisions showed a larger household cushion than previously estimated, but August's combination still left consumption growing faster than current purchasing power. Navy Federal Credit Union's Heather Long described the gap between spending and income as a test of consumers' continuing resilience.

The revised growth accounts reinforced the demand picture. Q2 GDP expanded at a 2.2% seasonally adjusted annual rate, above the 1.5% consensus and revised up from the previously reported 1.5%. Investment, consumption and government outlays accounted for the upward revision, and Q1 growth was also revised higher. Consumer spending in Q2 grew at its fastest pace since the end of 2024. The stronger historical growth estimate and August's realized spending increased confidence that the economy could withstand restrictive borrowing costs.

September ADP employment supplied a separate, more recent labor observation. Private payrolls increased 90,000, the most in three months, versus the 70,000 consensus. August was revised to 36,000 from 38,000. The improvement did not establish the outcome of Friday's official employment release, but it weakened the case for treating slowing hiring as an already accelerating contraction. Together, ADP and the spending data helped long yields recover their upward momentum after the initial inflation-driven rally at the front end.

During Wednesday's trading, the 30-year yield rose as much as 6 basis points to 5.63%, its highest since 2002. Oxford Economics' John Canavan linked the steeper curve to the stronger activity figures and investors' reluctance to make large adjustments before payrolls. Natixis rates strategist John Briggs saw weak underlying buying interest, while Fort Washington's Dan Carter argued that investors already positioned for lower yields might have limited capacity to add more bonds. These assessments explained why a reduced chance of an October increase could coexist with further long-end losses.

Bloomberg's September 30 daily yield observations put the two-year at 4.89%, up 1.2 basis points, the 10-year at 5.29%, up 5.3, and the 30-year at 5.64%, up 7.2. The 2s10s spread widened 4.1 basis points to 40, while 2s30s widened 6 to 75. At 10 years, real yields increased 2.4 basis points to 2.915% and inflation compensation rose 2.9 to 2.375%. The day's nominal increase therefore included higher real borrowing costs and higher breakeven inflation, rather than only one of those components.

The policy reassessment concerned the next meeting more than the full tightening cycle. Following the inflation release and Tuesday's patient message from New York Fed President John Williams, Goldman Sachs economists moved their forecast for the next increase from October to December. Traders nevertheless retained expectations for at least three increases over the following year. PNC chief economist Gus Faucher judged that the Fed could wait for now while still expecting further tightening. No new Wednesday policy statement was needed to produce that shift: the fresh information was the inflation and activity combination.

Mortgage financing showed the restraint already reaching households. The Mortgage Bankers Association's 30-year fixed contract rate increased 18 basis points to 7.30% in the week ended September 25, its sixth consecutive weekly rise and highest since November 2023. Five-year adjustable mortgage rates increased 37 basis points to 6.47%, a more than two-year high. Purchase applications fell 4.3% to their lowest since April 2025, and refinancing applications declined another 8.7%, extending a retreat that began in mid-August.

First American economist Mark Fleming said the widening gap between existing mortgages at 3% or 4% and new rates above 7% would keep more owners in their current homes. His expectation of sticky house prices depended on the absence of a major downturn forcing sales. The immediate effect was therefore weaker transaction and refinancing activity, not necessarily a proportionate fall in property values. Strong aggregate spending was coexisting with a visibly constrained rate-sensitive sector.

Oil added to the difficulty of extrapolating August's inflation relief. WTI stood at $90.16 at the end of the fixed-income session, up 0.87%, and Brent at $103.58, up 0.97%. JPMorgan's new shipping estimate put the 10-day average of Middle East crude exports at 17.5 million barrels a day, 98% of pre-war levels; Goldman Sachs separately assessed flows as returning toward normal. The improvement quantified a broader recovery beyond the already restored Saudi pipeline, but continued shipping risks left delivered supply and energy prices unsettled.

Iraq's state marketer illustrated the remaining unevenness by offering October contractual crude supplies at discounts of as much as $37 a barrel to regional benchmarks. The concession sought to attract buyers despite shipping difficulties associated with Iraq's location farther from Hormuz. Recovering aggregate exports did not eliminate individual producers' logistical disadvantages. U.S. equities also failed to sustain their initial response to the inflation news: the S&P 500 lost 0.25%, reversing an intraday gain of as much as 0.7%, while the Nasdaq 100 added 0.23%.

## European Inflation Overshoots Meet Fiscal and Funding Risks

Germany, France and Italy each reported a fresh inflation acceleration, extending the breadth of Europe's energy shock. German annual inflation reached 3.3% in September, above the 3.2% median forecast and the highest in almost three years. Energy drove the increase, while the national underlying measure remained at 2.4%. Muted demand for workers, with unemployment rising during a month that normally brings post-summer hiring, offered little immediate support for a wage-led escalation.

France's annual rate rose to 3.4%, its fastest pace in more than two years, and Italy's reached 4.1%, the highest since 2023. Both exceeded expectations. French energy costs increased 21.2% from a year earlier. Some pressure appeared outside fuel: services inflation accelerated to 2.2% from 1.9%, while food rose 1.5%, up from 1.1%, as fresh-produce prices increased after heat waves. Those components qualified the description of a purely isolated energy shock without demonstrating a generalized wage-price spiral.

The ECB debate remained focused on that distinction. Bloomberg Economics' Simona Delle Chiaie expected officials to hold for now and deliver a final increase in December, arguing that the decisive question was energy's passage into core inflation and that evidence remained limited. Greece's Yannis Stournaras and Malta's Alexander Demarco, both relatively dovish policymakers, did not rule out October. Their openness contrasted with economists and traders favoring December, leaving the timing unsettled even as the fresh national readings strengthened the case for another increase this year.

German bonds gained during Wednesday's European trading despite the headline overshoots. The two-year yield fell 8 basis points to 3.22%, and the 10-year declined 6 to 3.57%. Markets assessed the chance of a quarter-point ECB move on October 29 at roughly a third, while still allowing as much as 90 basis points of tightening by next autumn. LB Macro's Simon Harvey disagreed with the low near-term pricing, putting his own probability near 50% because of the inflation readings and energy outlook. A calmer immediate policy timetable thus remained compatible with substantial tightening over a longer horizon.

French debt underperformed that broader rally. The 10-year premium over Germany edged above 120 basis points, and OATs traded 22 basis points above comparable Italian bonds, the widest such gap since the euro area's creation. The incremental deterioration came alongside the new inflation surprise and polling pointing to a Marine Le Pen-Jean-Luc Melenchon presidential runoff next year. Natixis strategist Theophile Legrand linked the intensifying political premium to that polling. Over the quarter, French 10-year yields increased 1.15 percentage points to 4.8%, their worst quarterly performance since at least 1999.

ECB President Christine Lagarde addressed a specific part of that political debate in a Wednesday interview. She rejected Melenchon's proposed cancellation of debt held by central banks as financially dangerous and technically uncertain, warning that nonpayment could deter lenders or raise the rates they demand and would breach European treaties. Her objection concerned the financing consequences of the proposal, not an announced change in France's debt treatment. Lagarde also left open an exit a few months before her term ends in October 2027, while saying she would remain in office into 2027 and had made no specific announcement.

Italy's fiscal response introduced a different pending choice. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said she would ask the European Commission for additional budget flexibility to support households and businesses facing higher energy bills. She planned to raise the issue at next week's finance ministers meeting in Luxembourg and the following EU Council meeting. Italy's confirmed 2025 deficit of 3.1% of GDP leaves it under the Excessive Deficit Procedure, complicating additional assistance. The request was not an agreed relaxation of borrowing limits, but it showed how the inflation shock was bringing fiscal support back into the discussion as market financing grew more expensive.

Poland's preliminary September inflation rose to 4% from 3.4%, matching the median forecast but reaching a 15-month high and exceeding the central bank's 2.5% target plus or minus 1 percentage point. Higher fuel costs and the end of a price cap contributed to the pressure. Governor Adam Glapinski had favored unchanged rates at 3.75% this year and possibly into mid-2027, while council member Ludwik Kotecki envisaged discussions in October and a possible November increase if projections showed inflation staying above 4% for longer. ING Bank Slaski and Bank Pekao had both changed their forecasts to expect increases; the zloty strengthened 0.2% against the euro Wednesday.

The Bank of England's quarterly financial-stability assessment added a funding concern distinct from the inflation releases. Hedge-fund leverage in gilts was stable but elevated, and the central bank warned that interconnections between sovereign bonds, corporate debt and AI-related assets could make several vulnerabilities crystallize together. Sterling money-market data showed gilt repo dealers' net cash lending to non-bank financial institutions had doubled since 2023 to GBP200 billion. Greater reliance on gilts for funding increases the potential for stress to spread when leveraged positions must be unwound.

The BOE also warned that AI valuations could suffer a sharper correction than July's episode. That earlier shock had involved position unwinding and deleveraging without spillover into core markets. The new concern was that growth expectations now depend partly on AI productivity, so a reassessment could affect sovereign debt as well as technology shares. Some private-credit markets remained vulnerable to tighter financing conditions. The bank nevertheless judged households resilient and banks well capitalized, preserving a distinction between market vulnerabilities and an already impaired banking system.

Further analysis supported the BOE's July proposal to relax the absolute bank leverage cap. Officials considered planned gilt-market reforms a better response to the financing risks and intended to consult in early 2027, while retaining the option to increase leverage-ratio buffers by 25 basis points if risks changed. The combination was not a finding that leverage no longer mattered; it assigned the problem to market-specific reforms rather than automatically tightening the broad balance-sheet constraint.

New equity-market analysis provided another view of the same possible cross-market adjustment. Macro Risk Advisors found the gap between single-stock volatility and index calm at its widest since the dot-com collapse in 2000. Cboe's Mandy Xu said roughly 40% of the S&P 500's largest 100 stocks had inverted call skew, reflecting unusually strong upside demand. Macro Risk Advisors' Dean Curnutt argued that a cutback in AI spending because of data-center debt concerns could make previously offsetting stock moves converge into a broad decline. That was a risk assessment, not an observed spending retrenchment.

## Paramount Secures Financing as Issuers Tailor Their Terms

Banks completed roughly $52 billion of syndication for Paramount Skydance's Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, converting the week's evolving order books into long-term funding. The company sold $30 billion of dollar investment-grade debt, $12.4 billion-equivalent of junk bonds and $9.46 billion of loans, according to people familiar with the transaction. Apollo, Bank of America and Citigroup led the offering. The $110 billion acquisition's financing could be placed, but at an unusually high absolute cost.

Yield premiums on the eight-part senior-bond sale narrowed during syndication, while the 2066 maturity still offered almost 9%. Three senior notes yielded more than 8%; only two U.S. investment-grade notes had been issued at such yields earlier this year. That contrast captured the difference between an improved credit concession during marketing and expensive underlying long-term rates. A narrower premium did not undo the rise in the benchmark cost of money.

The speculative-grade offering comprised $11.4 billion of dollar bonds in three parts and a EUR885 million five-year note. A 10-year dollar tranche yielded about 9.13%, while the euro note priced at 7%. The earlier eight-year euro tranche had been dropped. Junk-bond pricing remained broadly consistent with initial discussions, unlike the tightening in senior-bond premiums. The completed loan financing included $8.5 billion in dollars and EUR850 million, with interest margins of 2.75 percentage points over the respective benchmarks.

The final terms made Paramount's already demanding deleveraging task more concrete. Its $6 billion annual savings goal within three years must support a post-acquisition debt load exceeding $87 billion, according to CreditSights. Those are the operating and balance-sheet conditions against which the expensive completed financing will be judged. The senior-debt rating split also remains relevant: Fitch and S&P assign investment-grade ratings, while Moody's rates even the first-lien debt below investment grade. The apparent size of the high-grade transaction therefore does not imply unanimous agency confidence in the merged borrower's leverage or execution.

Other issuers obtained funding through changes in structure rather than simply accepting a higher senior-bond yield. Clearlake raised $1 billion in a collateralized fund obligation after revising its collateral and reducing leverage in discussions with investors. The vehicle holds $600 million of private-credit exposure, $200 million in a private-equity secondaries fund and another $200 million private-equity fund stake. Against those assets, it raised $775 million in Class A, B and C debt and $225 million in equity, with Goldman Sachs the sole structuring and placement agent.

The safest Clearlake bonds priced at 285 basis points over SOFR, 15 basis points below initial pricing. Class C pays 800 basis points over SOFR, while the first-loss equity portion is expected to generate an internal rate of return around 18%. Investors had resisted the leverage in an earlier structure holding three credit funds and two other private funds. The improvement in senior pricing consequently followed a substantive change in collateral and capital structure, not just a stronger order book for an unchanged deal. The securitization also gives insurers access to fund exposures they may be unable to hold directly as private equity.

Remy Cointreau used a debut hybrid to protect its investment-grade standing while pursuing a turnaround. Its EUR250 million subordinated bond, first callable after five years, priced at 6.75%, compared with initial indications of 7%-7.25%. Orders exceeded EUR695 million, more than 2.7 times the offering. Moody's rates the spirits group Baa3 with a negative outlook, making the partial equity treatment available for hybrids particularly valuable despite their higher cost than ordinary senior debt.

The relative price of that equity credit was also favorable compared with history. ICE index data put the average hybrid premium over senior bonds around 74 basis points, versus a long-term average near 120. Remy still faces weak cognac and premium-spirits demand, tariffs and changing drinking habits, even after stronger-than-expected first-quarter sales growth. CEO Franck Marilly's turnaround and portfolio review must address those operating pressures; the hybrid changes the rating treatment of funding rather than resolving them.

Leveraged lenders obtained a more explicit contractual concession in financing Platinum Equity's acquisition of a stake in Nestle's water business. Newly reported terms of the EUR2.8 billion deal included an omniblocker, intended to prevent preferential transactions with selected creditors at others' expense. Banks led by Bank of America and Deutsche Bank increased margins on the euro and dollar loans by as much as 1 percentage point to 4 percentage points over benchmarks, and the seven-year loans were offered at 97% of face value. The debt priced Friday for the jointly owned business, now called Peranel.

The protection is unusual for buyout financing and goes beyond a price concession: it addresses the risk that a subsequent liability-management deal changes relative creditor treatment. The terms show investors receiving both greater contractual protection and higher compensation. Elsewhere in securitization, Polar Asset Management launched an oversubscribed C$430 million Canadian residential mortgage-backed deal, White Bear RMBS I LP, Series 2026-1. Its uninsured first-lien, fixed-rate mortgages have a weighted-average loan-to-value ratio of 71.1%, with CMLS Financial servicing the transaction. Demand remained available for specified collateral even as unsecured and leveraged borrowers faced more expensive terms.

## Municipal Buyers Return as Weak Corporate Credits Deteriorate

Municipal bonds broke their nearly two-week slide with a rally that contrasted sharply with long Treasuries. At 4 p.m. New York time, the benchmark 10-year municipal yield was down 11 basis points at 4.11%, its biggest price gain since April 2025 and first gain since September 17. The 30-year municipal yield fell 6 basis points to 5.19%. Belle Haven's Dora Lee viewed the move as a correction from oversold conditions but remained uncertain about its durability with further Fed tightening still ahead.

The rebound began to reopen the primary market. Nashville and Davidson County's Convention Center Authority offered about $790 million of bonds after postponing pricing the preceding week, with the transaction slightly larger than previously planned. Absolute yields were drawing buyers back, according to Cavanal Hill's Leslie Martin. New flow figures showed more than $3 billion entering Vanguard's VTEB municipal ETF over the past month, its strongest monthly inflow since 2022. That demand was appearing while the market was still absorbing extraordinary September losses, not only after prices stabilized.

At the weakest end of corporate credit, the direction was the opposite. CCC-rated bonds traded at a 1,007-basis-point spread over Treasuries Wednesday, up from 860 at September's start and above the conventional 1,000-basis-point distressed threshold for the first time since the March 2023 banking crisis. Broad U.S. high-yield spreads widened modestly over the day. The CCC milestone was more severe than that aggregate description and highlighted the borrowers most exposed to refinancing at higher rates.

Charles Schwab's Collin Martin said the economy was performing reasonably well without enough strength to remove the weakest issuers' sensitivity to borrowing costs. Smaller leveraged companies also have less room to absorb expensive energy if they cannot pass costs on. Barclays found substantial dispersion within CCCs: more than half of the worst performers were in technology, media and telecommunications, especially cable and satellite businesses. CCC issuers represent about 8.5% of the high-yield index, down from 9.7% a year earlier, while higher-rated spreads have remained relatively steadier. The deterioration was concentrated rather than equally distributed through corporate credit.

Leslie's supplied a new realized restructuring. The pool retailer filed a prearranged Chapter 11 case in the Southern District of Texas Wednesday, with a support agreement intended to eliminate about $685 million of debt, roughly 90% of its borrowings, and transfer control to creditors. The agreement includes commitments for $90 million of new-money debtor-in-possession financing. The company plans to continue ordinary operations and aims to emerge in early 2027; it also announced 76 store closures and further review of its property footprint.

The filing followed an unsuccessful attempt to extend maturities and negotiations with creditors including Grey Helm, Axar, Cerberus and Contrarian. Weather disruptions, higher input costs and pressure on household finances had challenged the pool industry. Leslie's listed assets of $500 million-$1 billion and liabilities of $1 billion-$10 billion in its petition. The new financing and proposed reduction address its balance sheet through court proceedings rather than merely moving repayments into a later year.

Hertz was pursuing the less drastic route. PJT Partners had contacted debt investors over recent weeks about a possible amend-and-extend transaction, according to people familiar with the discussions. Hertz has a $200 million bond carrying a 4.63% coupon due December 1 and $2.7 billion of loans maturing in 2028. Its reported liquidity of almost $1 billion in August exceeded the December maturity, so the talks did not establish an inability to make that payment. Heavy vehicle depreciation and volatile finances nevertheless make the terms of any broader extension consequential.

Brightline changed the proposed treatment of its corporate-bond creditors. A Wednesday filing gave those investors at least 4.75% of the reorganized company's equity, governance rights, warrants for potential additional ownership and a right of first offer to supply capital to future Brightline entities. The corporate bonds, roughly $1.1 billion carrying an 11% rate, rely on revenue remaining after about $2.2 billion of senior municipal debt. They had initially been excluded from the restructuring proposal. The equity and participation rights therefore represent a specific concession to junior holdouts rather than another announcement of the bankruptcy itself.

New reporting also identified Diameter Capital Partners, Redwood Capital and FourSixThree Capital as buyers of the approximately $190 million senior uninsured municipal portfolio that Nuveen sold at 45 cents on the dollar. On Wednesday, that debt traded at 55 cents. The price recovery followed the already reported all-or-nothing sale and did not reverse its realized transaction terms. Brightline's plan includes $258 million of bankruptcy financing from Assured Guaranty and other municipal investors. The improved terms for corporate creditors and different price for senior debt show separate developments at distinct ranks of the capital structure.

Bank regulation brought an independent institutional change. The Fed board approved two final stress-test rules by a 6-1 vote, requiring public input on scenarios and material model changes and updating the scenario framework, calendar and global-market-shock component. From 2028, stress capital buffers will average the two most recent annual tests for banks participating in both years. The Fed estimates roughly a 50% reduction in annual capital-requirement volatility without a material change in aggregate capital requirements.

Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said the framework would remain resilient through more transparent, granular and risk-sensitive testing. Governor Michael Barr dissented, arguing that the rules would significantly weaken tests and bank resilience. The Fed separately sought input on better reflecting differences in banks' fee-income business models. The decision changes how capital requirements evolve across years, while the disagreement concerns whether greater predictability comes at the expense of the test's ability to expose risk.

The Fed also faced a renewed governance dispute after its inspector general found no criminal wrongdoing or administrative misconduct in the headquarters renovation, but identified management failures behind the cost increase to $2.4 billion from an initial $1.3 billion budget in 2020. President Donald Trump demanded former chair Jerome Powell's resignation from the board and asked Attorney General Todd Blanche to review the findings. Chair Kevin Warsh said the Fed would implement recommendations, appoint an independent cost auditor and place the General Services Administration in charge of project execution. The watchdog's conclusions and Trump's reaction were distinct: the report identified oversight deficiencies without substantiating the criminal accusation.

## Asian Activity and Emerging-Market Policy Diverge

China's September activity surveys improved without producing a comparable repricing of its bond market. Official manufacturing PMI rose to 50.1 from 49.8, matching forecasts and returning to expansion for the first time since June. The non-manufacturing measure unexpectedly reached 50.2, while construction activity ended an eight-month decline. RatingDog's manufacturing survey rose more than expected to 52.1, a five-month high, and its services PMI increased to 51.6 from 51.4. The official and private measures both improved, although the private manufacturing sample has been more responsive to resilient exports.

Government bonds and the yuan were broadly steady after the releases and the latest targeted support. The 10-year government yield was around 1.67% Wednesday. Fresh policy detail included a 25-basis-point reduction in the one-year pledged supplementary lending rate to 1.5% and an additional CNY200 billion quota for relending supporting technological innovation and equipment upgrades. These measures lowered financing costs or expanded funding in selected areas, rather than announcing a broad reduction in market rates.

The response remained limited because access to cheaper credit is not the same as willingness to borrow. Barclays economists led by Yingke Zhou identified credit demand, rather than its price, as the central constraint. Mortgage subsidies already announced for qualifying buyers begin October 1, with eligibility caps on floor space and value concentrating the benefit in lower-tier cities. Morgan Stanley's Robin Xing argued that household deleveraging and local-government pressure from weak land revenue could limit the effect. The improving September activity measures thus coexist with policies designed to protect the growth floor, not evidence of a comprehensive property recovery.

China's repo market showed progress on another dimension of bond demand. Offshore institutions conducted CNY1.2 trillion of monthly repos in August, more than double CNY573 billion a year earlier. Foreign investors hold about CNY3.2 trillion in domestic bonds, and the new financing access improves their ability to use those securities for liquidity. Outright repos, which transfer ownership rather than freeze collateral in the seller's account, accounted for 23% of foreign settlement volumes, versus about 4% a year earlier.

Participation is still narrow. Offshore investors' repo trades represented only 1.2% of total market volume despite their roughly 2% ownership share of onshore bonds. Choice between English-law global agreements and Chinese-law local contracts creates friction over bankruptcy treatment, operational rules and close-out netting; GMRA negotiations typically take three to six months, according to Ashurst Perkins Coie's Priscilla Chen. Low Chinese yields also limit foreign demand. Market access and collateral utility are improving faster than the international appeal of the underlying return.

Vale's potential debut panda bond illustrated that low-yield market's attraction to borrowers. The Brazilian miner is considering up to CNY3.5 billion, about $522 million, with roadshows in the week of October 19 and marketing as early as November. Possible three-, five- and 10-year maturities remain subject to investor feedback. Vale Overseas would issue the bonds with a parent guarantee. Corporate and sovereign panda issuance has reached CNY245 billion this year, up 78%, with average coupons of 1.88%, the lowest on record. The proposed transaction would diversify Vale's funding in a market accounting for about half its revenue; it is not yet a completed sale.

Japan's two-year auction provided a realized demand test. Bid coverage rose to 3.89 times from 2.97 at the previous sale, above the 12-month average of 3.75. The difference between the average and lowest accepted prices narrowed to 0.014 from 0.034, and futures pared losses after the result. The two-year yield fell 1.5 basis points to 1.945%. SMBC Nikko's Miki Den attributed the solid reception to high yields, with buyers responding even as another BOJ increase remained possible. Wednesday's overnight swaps assigned roughly a 23% chance to an October move and almost fully priced 25 basis points by December.

In Australia, fresh housing and inflation observations sharpened the constraint on extending the tightening cycle. August inflation reached 4%, above the RBA's 2%-3% target, while Cotality reported a sixth consecutive monthly decline in national home values. Prices were 5.2% below their March peak, with Sydney down 8.6% from February and Melbourne down 7.2% from November. Seven of eight capital cities were falling, with Darwin the exception and regional areas still rising. Expensive homes in Sydney and Melbourne had lost more than 10% from their peaks.

The financial sensitivity is substantial: household debt is equivalent to about 178% of annual disposable income, and most mortgages have variable rates. Commonwealth Bank reported a 15% fall in total mortgage applications and a 28% drop in investor applications since May. From July 2027, negative-gearing deductions will be restricted to newly built homes, while an inflation-adjusted purchase price will replace the 50% capital-gains discount. Those announced tax changes are a prospective additional constraint on investor demand, alongside the current effect of the 4.6% cash rate.

Forecasts differ on the scale of the downturn. Westpac's Matthew Hassan expects a 7.3% peak-to-trough national decline, Commonwealth Bank's Trent Saunders 9%, and HSBC's Paul Bloxham 13%, with a 17% fall in Sydney. Schroders bought three-year bonds Tuesday, and its Australian fixed-income head Kellie Wood expected easing in 2027 as the inflation shock matured and growth risks became more important. Aberdeen's Adam McCabe still expected another increase because of persistent inflation and wanted clearer economic softening. The fresh housing figures add weight to the growth constraint without removing the above-target inflation observation.

Indian assets faced pressure from a less favorable external balance. Foreigners sold $1.1 billion of index-eligible sovereign bonds in September, heading for the largest monthly outflow since March after record June inflows, and $2.1 billion of equities after two months of purchases. The 10-year sovereign yield reached a two-year high this week. Higher oil costs burden an import-dependent economy, while rising developed-market yields make local returns less competitive and currency hedging more expensive. Aberdeen's Fesa Wibawa regarded the selling chiefly as part of the global bond correction, rather than a wholesale reassessment of India.

The retreat came despite banks attracting $133 billion through the special diaspora deposit program. Those dollars were swapped with the RBI and briefly lifted reserves to a record $785.7 billion, but the central bank continued selling dollars to support the rupee. A weak monsoon, the poorest in more than a decade amid a powerful El Nino, added a separate risk to crops, reservoirs and food prices. The combination complicates policy support: stronger external buffers coexist with current foreign selling and fresh domestic supply concerns.

Colombia delivered a surprise quarter-point increase to 12.25%, its highest policy rate since 2024. Four board members supported the move, two favored holding and one wanted a half-point increase. Twenty-two of 29 analysts had expected no change; five forecast a larger half-point move and only two the increase actually delivered. Governor Leonardo Villar said restrictive policy was consistent with a declining inflation path in 2027. August inflation had accelerated to 6.24%, well above the 3% target plus or minus 1 percentage point.

The hike occurred against weaker activity, not accelerating growth. Urban unemployment unexpectedly reached 9.1% in August, and July activity, manufacturing and retail sales all fell short of forecasts. Finance Minister Miguel Gomez's first policy meeting came with investors awaiting details of promised fiscal cuts. The government's warning that next year's deficit could exceed 9% of GDP and its IMF discussions leave fiscal credibility important to the inflation outlook. The vote showed a majority choosing additional restraint despite clearer economic cooling.

Zambia moved decisively in the opposite direction. Governor Denny Kalyalya announced a reduction from 13.25% to 10.75%, the fourth consecutive cut and largest since at least 2012. September inflation eased to 6.1% from 6.2%, and projections placed it inside the 6%-8% target band into 2028. Forecast annual averages were lowered by about 1 percentage point to 6.7% this year and 6% next year, before 6.3% in the first half of 2028. The kwacha's almost 13% appreciation and expected stable grain prices supported that outlook.

Zambia's reserves increased to $6 billion at July's end from $5.8 billion in June, enough for 4.5 months of imports, with mining taxes and project inflows contributing. The bank expects growth of 5.3% this year, 6% in 2027 and 7.1% in 2028. Its favorable projections retain important risks from El Nino and the Middle East conflict, while the moratorium on fuel taxes and VAT zero-rating expires September 30. The substantial cut relied on domestic inflation and currency conditions different from those confronting Colombia.

Sri Lanka held its overnight rate at 8.75% for a second meeting, as six of 11 surveyed economists expected; the others anticipated increases of 25-50 basis points. The central bank said earlier tightening was working and medium-term inflation expectations remained anchored, despite August inflation of 8% versus a 5% target. It projects high-single-digit inflation through Q1 2027 before convergence toward target and stands ready to act if pressure intensifies or expectations weaken. Q2 growth slowed to 4.2% from 5.1%, adding a recovery constraint to the energy-import risk.

Mozambique also held, keeping its Mimo rate at 9.25% for a fourth meeting. New Governor Felisberto Navalha cited energy, climate and weak-growth risks despite August inflation easing to 6.5%. Diesel pump prices have risen more than 40% in recent months, and foreign-exchange shortages are disrupting imports. The Finance Ministry expects only 0.6% growth this year and projects wages plus debt service absorbing 96% of 2027 revenue. An IMF-funded program could require greater currency flexibility; S&P expects modest metical depreciation through 2029, another potential source of price pressure.

Gabon, meanwhile, mandated BofA to begin investor meetings Wednesday for a proposed $580 million dollar bond with an eight-year final maturity, only two months after raising $920 million. The offering comes during talks on a funded IMF program. Its 2031 bonds fell 1.2 cents to 84.3 at 12:26 p.m. London time, a sixth daily decline, and 2029 notes lost 0.7 cent to 94.4. Renewed pressure followed the draft budget's plan for CFr1.1 trillion, about $1.9 billion, in international borrowing, offsetting earlier enthusiasm over an audit showing debt about a fifth lower than previously estimated.

Higher-rated emerging borrowers have also been expanding alternative-currency access. Swiss-franc issuance reached about $3.9 billion through Monday, almost triple the corresponding 2025 amount, although small beside $610 billion raised in hard currencies overall. Chile's debut CHF380 million two-part sale established five- and 10-year benchmarks, with demand almost entirely from Swiss investors. Gramercy's Petar Atanasov saw the market as most accessible to A- and BBB-category borrowers, while Aberdeen's Viktor Szabo noted that lower nominal coupons can lose some advantage after dollar hedging. Diversification increases funding options without replacing the deeper dollar and euro markets.

## Forward Market Significance

October 1 manufacturing ISM, due at 10 a.m. New York time, is expected at 55 after 54.6. It will test whether September's hiring improvement and the stronger consumption picture extend into factory activity. Friday's official employment release at 8:30 a.m. is expected to show 90,000 September payroll gains after 162,000, with unemployment unchanged at 4.1%. ADP's fresh upside surprise makes the official breadth of hiring important: another resilient observation would support the economy's capacity to absorb high rates, while pronounced weakness would challenge the long end's growth assumption.

October 5 services ISM follows at 10 a.m., with the published forecast at 54 after 55.4. Its relevance is distinct from manufacturing because spending and services prices remained firm in the PCE detail. The question is whether that demand persists as income growth lags consumption and higher mortgage costs restrain housing turnover. These releases will arrive before the October 28 Fed decision, whose near-term tightening probability fell Wednesday without eliminating expectations of later increases.

Friday's euro-area inflation release is expected at 3.7%, with the fresh German, French and Italian overshoots creating upside risk. Core inflation and evidence of broader pass-through matter more to the October-versus-December ECB choice than another energy-driven headline alone. France's October 1 budget presentation poses a separate sovereign test after OATs edged above 120 basis points over bunds: the proposals and their political reception must meet investors' concern about the financing path, not just the continent-wide inflation outlook.

The U.S. Treasury plans a Thursday buyback accepting up to $6 billion of securities maturing in 10-20 years. Previous long-term operations accepted less than the announced maximum, making the actual take-up relevant to the liquidity effect. Wells Fargo's Angelo Manolatos said buybacks had their greatest influence on liquidity and spreads, while a negative growth catalyst would probably be needed for a sustained decline in long rates. The operation is a planned repurchase, not an auction or an already completed reduction in supply.

Corporate attention now shifts from Paramount's marketing to the burden of the financing it secured, while Brightline's promised equity and participation rights remain part of a court-supervised exit plan. Wednesday's municipal rebound also gives postponed borrowers a new opportunity to price, with Nashville's return an immediate example. The contrast to CCC distress leaves the durability of demand dependent on the borrower and terms rather than on a universal recovery in fixed income.

Energy remains an independent test. The newly estimated recovery to 98% of pre-war crude exports must be sustained amid shipping risk, and Iraqi discounts show that restored aggregate flows do not resolve every delivery constraint. Oil's Wednesday rise, even after those estimates, leaves the current fuel shock relevant beyond the softer August inflation result. Whether relief reaches refined products and then household and business costs will shape how long central banks can defer another increase.

section_summaries.summary: Quarter-end demand was increasingly selective: municipal bonds staged their strongest 10-year rally in more than a year, CCC borrowers crossed the distressed-spread threshold, and Paramount completed costly acquisition financing. Europe's inflation overshoots complicated ECB timing, while China's modest activity rebound did not establish a recovery in domestic credit demand.

section_summaries.market_read: Goldman Sachs shifted its next Fed increase forecast from October to December, while traders still expected at least three increases over the following year.
section_summaries.section_title: Softer PCE Changes Fed Timing, Not Long-Bond Demand
section_summaries.summary: Core PCE's 0.2% monthly increase reduced immediate tightening expectations, but real spending rose 0.6% and ADP hiring exceeded forecasts. The 30-year yield reached 5.64% as weak buying interest limited the inflation rally; both real yields and inflation compensation rose at 10 years. Income lagged consumption, mortgage applications weakened, and firmer services prices and oil left the inflation outlook unsettled.

section_summaries.section_title: European Inflation Overshoots Meet Fiscal and Funding Risks
section_summaries.summary: German, French and Italian inflation exceeded forecasts, but German bonds rallied as near-term ECB tightening remained uncertain. France's 10-year premium over Germany moved above 120 basis points amid political risk, while Italy sought budget flexibility for energy support. Poland's inflation reopened debate over tightening. The BOE warned that elevated gilt leverage and links to corporate debt and AI assets could transmit funding stress.

section_summaries.section_title: Paramount Secures Financing as Issuers Tailor Their Terms
section_summaries.summary: Paramount completed roughly $52 billion of acquisition financing; narrower senior-bond premiums still left its 2066 maturity yielding almost 9%. Its $6 billion annual savings goal must support debt exceeding $87 billion. Clearlake revised collateral and reduced leverage to secure funding, Remy Cointreau sold a EUR250 million hybrid to protect its investment-grade standing, and Peranel's lenders obtained higher margins and protection against preferential creditor deals.

section_summaries.section_title: Municipal Buyers Return as Weak Corporate Credits Deteriorate
section_summaries.summary: The 10-year municipal yield fell 11 basis points to 4.11%, helping Nashville return with about $790 million of bonds. CCC spreads reached 1,007 basis points as refinancing pressure intensified. Leslie's filed Chapter 11 with a plan to eliminate about $685 million of debt, Hertz explored maturity extensions, and Brightline offered corporate creditors at least 4.75% of reorganized equity plus participation rights. New Fed stress-test rules aim to reduce annual capital-requirement volatility without materially changing aggregate requirements.

section_summaries.market_read: China's repo access improved collateral utility for foreign investors, but low yields and contractual friction continued to limit participation.
section_summaries.section_title: Asian Activity and Emerging-Market Policy Diverge
section_summaries.summary: China's manufacturing PMI returned to expansion at 50.1, but targeted funding support faced weak credit demand. Japan's two-year auction drew stronger bids, while falling Australian home prices constrained policy despite 4% inflation. Foreign selling pressured Indian bonds as oil and hedging costs rose. Colombia unexpectedly raised its rate to 12.25%; Zambia cut to 10.75% on easing inflation and a stronger currency. Sri Lanka and Mozambique held rates, while panda and Swiss-franc issuance expanded funding options.

U.S. ISM surveys and Friday's payrolls will test the resilient-demand case behind higher long yields. Euro-area core inflation will inform ECB timing, while France's budget faces a separate sovereign-financing test. Treasury's planned buyback may improve liquidity rather than sustain a rate rally. Paramount's financing burden, municipal demand and sustained oil-delivery relief remain unresolved; recovering crude exports have not yet settled energy pass-through.

overall_summary.headline: Long Treasuries fall as resilient demand outweighs softer inflation's relief on Fed timing
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Long Treasuries lost ground on September 30 even after August core PCE rose just 0.2%, below the 0.3% consensus, and swaps cut the probability of an October Fed increase to about 36% from roughly even odds. Two-year yields initially fell as much as 5 basis points to 4.82% before surrendering much of the decline. Real spending rose 0.6%, and September ADP payrolls increased 90,000 against a 70,000 forecast, sustaining the growth case while long-bond buying interest remained weak and corporate financing competed for capital. The 10-year yield reached 5.29% and the 30-year 5.64%, its highest level since 2002; higher real yields and inflation compensation both contributed to the 10-year move.

Demand diverged sharply by borrower. At 4 p.m. New York time, the 10-year municipal yield fell 11 basis points to 4.11%, its strongest rally since April 2025, while CCC spreads reached 1,007 basis points, crossing the distressed threshold. Paramount secured roughly $52 billion for its Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, but its 2066 senior bond still offered almost 9% despite narrower premiums.

German, French and Italian inflation overshoots left the ECB's October-versus-December timing unsettled, while France's political and financing risks pushed its 10-year premium over Germany above 120 basis points. China's activity surveys improved without a comparable bond repricing because domestic credit demand remained constrained. Oil rose despite estimated Middle East crude exports recovering to 98% of pre-war levels, leaving energy pass-through unresolved ahead of the next activity and inflation releases.
overall_summary.summary: Softer core PCE reduced the likelihood of an October Fed increase, but stronger spending and private hiring, weak long-bond buying interest and heavy corporate financing kept decades-long borrowing costs rising.
